title: "The dearest land"
hook: leaving, he says to Mecca: you are the dearest land to me, and if your people hadn't driven me out I'd never have left (Tirmidhi)

segments.voice: Yesterday, al-Amin's trusts returned. Your line was: trusts returned, even then. What did you give back? Day seven hundred sixty-five.

The city that just tried to kill him is behind him now. Its leaders mocked him. Its council voted on his death. Its young men waited at his door with swords. And as the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, leaves it, the hadith keep words he speaks to it. Not to the people. To the place itself. Two companions report what he said, and both reports are kept in the hadith collection of al-Tirmidhi. Today: Mecca.
screen: `THE CITY BEHIND HIM.` → `HE SPEAKS TO MECCA.` → `HE SPEAKS TO THE PLACE.`

segments.voice: In one report, from Abdullah ibn Adi, the Prophet stands at a spot in Mecca and says: by God, you are the best of God's earth, and the dearest of God's earth to God. And if I had not been driven out of you, I would never have left. In the other, from Ibn Abbas, he speaks more personally: how good you are as a land, and how dear you are to me. If my people had not driven me out, I would never have lived anywhere but you. Listen to the two halves of that. The first half is pure love: dearest, best, how good you are. The second half names exactly what happened, with no softening: I was driven out. He doesn't pretend he's leaving by choice. And he doesn't let what the people did turn into hatred for the place. The Qur'an uses the same plain language. It speaks of the town that drove you out. So here's a man saying goodbye honestly. Grief and love, and the truth about why, all in two sentences. Anyone who has left a hometown, a country, a house they grew up in, may know the shape of it. You can love a place and still be forced to leave it. You can say both things out loud. And the story doesn't end here. Mecca will come back into his life later. Here, he says goodbye.
screen: `THE DEAREST OF GOD'S EARTH.` · `IF I HADN'T BEEN DRIVEN OUT.` · `LOVE AND TRUTH TOGETHER.` · `THE TOWN THAT DROVE YOU OUT.` · then, large: `THE DEAREST LAND.`

segments.voice: The practice: say goodbye to a place you love. Sit, and breathe. Let a place come to you: a childhood home, a city you moved away from, a room that isn't yours anymore, a street, a kitchen, a country. Walk through it slowly in your mind. The light. The smell. Who was there. Notice if there's a reason you left that still stings, and let it be true without arguing with it. Then, silently or under your breath, tell the place what it was to you. In one or two plain sentences, the way he did. If you pray, you can thank God for that place. The bell holds the time.
Mecca. Leaving the city, the Prophet told it he would never have left if he hadn't been driven out, the dearest land to him. Today's word.
Your line: grief and love, both true. Today, tell someone about a place you love and had to leave, and say honestly why you left. Day seven hundred sixty-five.

howItsDone: Many Muslims quote the Prophet's farewell to Mecca when they speak of love for one's homeland, and Mecca remains the city Muslims face in prayer and travel to on pilgrimage.

fork.setup: you're leaving the city that tried to kill you. you stop at its edge. what do you say to it?
options: you are the dearest land to me.
fork.reveal: he told Mecca it was the dearest land, and that he would never have left if his people hadn't driven him out.

trapdoor: what you thought: he was glad to get away.
what it means: he said goodbye with love for the place and honesty about why he had to go.
what a scholar hears: two reports in Jami' al-Tirmidhi, from Abdullah ibn Adi and Ibn Abbas; the Qur'an speaks of the town that drove him out (47:13).

sources.ref: Jami' al-Tirmidhi 3925 (Abdullah ibn Adi ibn al-Hamra: the best and dearest of God's earth; if I had not been driven out I would not have left)
Jami' al-Tirmidhi 3926 (Ibn Abbas: how good you are as a land and how dear to me; if my people had not driven me out I would not have lived elsewhere)
Qur'an 47:13 (the township which drove you out)

notes: Tirmidhi numbers 3925 and 3926 as recalled; confirm numbering and that both are graded acceptable.
The Abdullah ibn Adi report places the words at al-Hazwara in Mecca, not necessarily on the night of the hijra; the script frames it as said while leaving, following the index. Confirm framing.
'Where he was born, where Khadijah is buried': confirm both are fitting to state here.
'Mecca will come back into his life, years from now' alludes to the later conquest without dating it.

Editor pass: cut the invented 'he stops, and turns' staging; cut 'where he was born, where Khadijah is buried' (not in the cited texts); 47:13 no longer said to be 'about that night'; 'will recognize' softened so the narrator doesn't tell listeners what they feel; cut the claim about what he did not know, and 'years from now'.

Audit pass: 'two companions remember' changed to 'report' (Ibn Abbas was a small child at the hijra); cut 'asleep in the dark' and 'tonight' staging, since the Abdullah ibn Adi report places him standing at al-Hazwara; howItsDone softened to 'many Muslims'.
